newsitem.title: USA: US Diagnostic says probe eyes disclosure.
newsitem.headline: US Diagnostic says probe eyes disclosure.

text.p: US Diagnostic Inc said on Monday that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's inquiry of the company's relationship with Coyote Consulting Financial Services LLC and Keith Greenberg is focused on the issue of disclosure.
"To the best of our knowledge, there are no other issues that the SEC is looking into," said Laurans Mendelson, the company's chairman of the board, in a telephone conference call Monday morning.
"They have not requested information in any other area," he said.

Earlier in the day, US Diagnostic said in a press release that the SEC and the Nasdaq Stock Market had initiated inquiries focusing on the company's relationship with Coyote and Greenberg and the adequacy of US Daignostic's disclosure concerning that relationship.

"To the best of our knowledge, (Greenberg) has never been a director and never been elected an officer of this company," Mendelson said. "He was connected with a company that has a consulting agreement with US Diagnostic."
Mendelson said that the investigation will reveal whether Greenberg ever held himself out to be an officer of the company.

In December, analysts at Bear Stearns said in a research note that Greenberg has pleaded guilty to fraud and conspiracy charges in U.S. District Court in 1994. The analysts said that they believed that Greenberg was a co-founder of US Diagnostic.
In response, US Diagnostic had said that Greenberg was not a co-founder of the company, but was given founding shares when the company was started in 1993.
